title: Marblo Store item manifest (marblo.yaml)
description: Every item in the Marblo ecosystem — skill, MCP server, agent, workflow, knowledge pack, harness, or bundle — is described by a marblo.yaml that validates against this schema. First-party items are plain, standards-native files that work standalone in Claude Code / Codex; this manifest is additive Store metadata, not a container. The Marblo app reads these manifests to build the Store index and to install items by tag or commit SHA.

localizedStrings.description: Translated display strings for one locale. Every field is optional and falls back independently: translate the name, the description, both, or neither. At least one field must be present — an empty locale object says nothing and is rejected so it cannot be mistaken for a translation that exists.

schema_version.description: Manifest schema version. Bump only on breaking changes to this schema.

id.description: Globally unique, stable, kebab-case identifier. Never reused for a different item.

name.description: Human-readable display name shown in the Store.

type.description: Store category. The executable types — skill, agent, workflow, mcp-server, harness — must declare `permissions` (see below).

version.description: SemVer of THIS manifest/item. For manifest-only external items, tracks the pinned upstream ref.

description.description: One or two sentences: what it does and when to install it.

i18n.description: OPTIONAL per-locale overlay for the two display strings. `name` and `description` above stay English — they are the base, and the base is what every item is reviewed and searched by. A client shows the entry matching the user's locale when one exists FOR THAT FIELD and the English base otherwise, field by field, so a partial translation is a real option rather than a broken one. Nothing here is ever required: most items carry no `i18n` block at all and display in English, which is a complete and supported state — the registry does not ask contributors to translate an item they cannot translate accurately. This block carries display strings only; `id`, `keywords`, and every install field stay locale-independent.

status.description: Lifecycle state; absent means `active`. `deprecated` = still installable but superseded. `revoked` = withdrawn for a security, licensing, or provenance reason — the app must refuse to install it and warn about it if already installed. Revocations are recorded in SECURITY-ADVISORIES.md; app-side enforcement lands in Phase 1a (see ROADMAP.md).

tier.description: official = maintained by Marblo; verified = external, reviewed & source-pinned; community = external, listed but not reviewed. NOTE: today this field is self-asserted by whoever writes the manifest, so it is a claim, not a guarantee — a `tier` in a file the contributor controls cannot certify itself. Phase 1a moves tier derivation into CI (from repo ownership and a maintainer-controlled trusted-publisher list) and the app will read the derived value, not this one. Until then, treat tier as an editorial label enforced by human review at merge time.

source.description: For external / manifest-only items: where the real code lives. Marblo installs from this pinned ref — it is NOT vendored into this repo. Required for every item whose publisher tier is not `official` (see allOf below).

ref.description: Immutable pin: a release tag (e.g. v1.7.0, 2026.07.29-1) or a full 40-character commit SHA. Moving branches (main, master, develop, HEAD) do not match this pattern and are rejected — what the Store installs has to be what was reviewed. If your tag does not fit the version-tag shape, pin the 40-hex commit SHA instead.

path.description: Subpath within the source repo, if not the root. When the item declares a `files` install, this must be the DIRECTORY the install.files entries are relative to.

harnesses.description: Which agent harnesses this item works with. `any` means it is harness-neutral — it needs nothing Marblo-specific.

permissions.description: Capabilities the item requests, surfaced to the user before install. REQUIRED for every executable type (skill, agent, workflow, mcp-server, harness): an empty array is a valid and meaningful declaration — 'this item asks for nothing' — whereas omission says nothing at all, and an omitted list must not be able to render as harmless. This is disclosure, not enforcement: Marblo shows what an item says it needs; it does not restrict what the item can do once installed. Scoped forms (e.g. network:outbound:<host>) land with the Phase 1a permission gate.

install.description: How the Marblo app installs this item, if it can. OPTIONAL: an item with no `install` block is listed and disclosed in the Store but has no install button — the app never guesses an install procedure from the other fields. The block is a kind-discriminated union and is deliberately narrow: it names WHICH package to run or WHICH files to copy, and it can never supply a shell command, an absolute path, a secret value, or a moving ref. Every rule below is re-enforced inside the app immediately before anything touches disk, so a manifest edited after review cannot widen what gets installed.

kind.description: `files` copies an allowlist of files out of this repo at the reviewed commit. `mcp-server` writes one entry into the harness MCP config. `shell` does not exist and never will — curl-pipe-bash is unreachable from the registry at any tier.

allOf.$comment: kind: files — copy an explicit allowlist into an app-controlled root.

root.description: Destination root, as an ENUM KEY the app maps to an absolute path — `claude-skills` resolves to the harness skills directory, `claude-agents` to its subagents directory. A manifest can never carry a path. The root is also bound to the item `type` (see allOf below): a skill cannot install itself into the agents tree, and an agent cannot install itself into the skills tree, so the category an item is listed under is the category it lands in.

dest.description: Directory name under `root`. Exactly one path segment: no `/`, no `\`, no `.`, no `..`. The app re-resolves and realpath-checks containment on top of this.

files.description: Explicit allowlist of files to copy. Nothing outside this list is ever written. For vendored (official) payloads the paths are relative to this manifest's directory; for source-referenced (community) payloads they are relative to `source.path` in the source repo at the pinned `source.ref` — the app builds the fetch URL itself and only ever talks to raw.githubusercontent.com.

integrity.description: Per-file digests, verified at install time. Required: without it, 'what the Store installs is what was reviewed' is an unbacked claim.

files.description: Map of the same relative paths listed in `files` to their lowercase hex sha256.

allOf.$comment: kind: mcp-server — register one server in the harness MCP config.

runner.description: Launcher enum, NOT a free-form command. `docker` and `binary` are reserved for a later phase and are rejected today rather than half-supported.

package.description: Exact, version-locked package: `name@x.y.z`. Dist-tags such as `@latest` are not a pin and are rejected.

args.description: Fixed extra arguments. Must be the same for every user — anything user-specific (a project ref, a workspace id) belongs in the user's own config, not here. `${...}` is rejected everywhere in this block: harness CLIs expand it at runtime, which would turn an argument into a secret-exfiltration channel.

mcp_key.description: Key written into the harness MCP config. May not shadow a key the app already ships built-in.

env_required.description: Environment variable NAMES the server needs. Values never appear in a manifest — the app writes only `${NAME}` and the user supplies the value. An empty array is a meaningful declaration ('needs no secrets'); harness/cloud credential names (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, AWS_*, …) are refused outright.

includes.description: For type=bundle only: ids of other registry items installed together.

license.description: SPDX license identifier for first-party items, or the upstream license for referenced ones.

allOf.$comment: A bundle must say what it bundles.
Executable types must declare permissions. An empty array is the way to say 'nothing'.
Anything not published by Marblo itself must be pinned to an immutable upstream ref. Without this, CONTRIBUTING's promise that 'the pinned source resolves' has nothing to resolve.

The install kind AND the destination root have to match the item type — a skill installs files into the skills tree, an agent installs files into the subagents tree, an MCP server registers a server. Only these three types are installable; the rest are list-and-disclose only. Binding root to type is what stops an item from being reviewed as one category and installed as another.
Registering an MCP server means a process launches on the user's machine on the next CLI start. Unreviewed (community) items do not get that. The app enforces the same gate independently.
